1  Introduction

This document briefly derives the basic algorithm by which the observations of a Virtual Reference Station (VRS) are generated.

Assume that at epoch t the rover u and the reference stations A, B and C almost simultaneously observe the L1 C/A signals broadcast by n satellites, and let λ denote the L1 C/A wavelength. The pseudorange observations are

ρui​=rui​+cdtu​−cdti+Iui​+Tui​+ϵui​ρAi​=rAi​+cdtA​−cdti+IAi​+TAi​+ϵAi​ρBi​=rBi​+cdtB​−cdti+IBi​+TBi​+ϵBi​ρCi​=rCi​+cdtC​−cdti+ICi​+TCi​+ϵCi​​
(1)

where

i=1,2,…,n
(2)

2  Observation model assumptions

Taking satellite j as the reference satellite and A as the master reference station, assume that the double-difference ionospheric delays are described by spatial functions FI​ evaluated at the station positions:

⎩⎨⎧​Iui​=FIi​(ru​,ri)IAi​=FIi​(rA​,ri)IBi​=FIi​(rB​,ri)ICi​=FIi​(rC​,ri)​,⎩⎨⎧​Iuj​=FIj​(ru​,rj)IAj​=FIj​(rA​,rj)IBj​=FIj​(rB​,rj)ICj​=FIj​(rC​,rj)​
(3)

and, in the same way, the tropospheric delays by functions FT​:

⎩⎨⎧​Tui​=FTi​(ru​,ri)TAi​=FTi​(rA​,ri)TBi​=FTi​(rB​,ri)TCi​=FTi​(rC​,ri)​,⎩⎨⎧​Tuj​=FTj​(ru​,rj)TAj​=FTj​(rA​,rj)TBj​=FTj​(rB​,rj)TCj​=FTj​(rC​,rj)​
(4)

The double-difference pseudorange observation equations of the rover and of the reference stations are then

ρuAij​=ruAij​+IuAij​+TuAij​+ϵuAij​ρBAij​=rBAij​+IBAij​+TBAij​+ϵBAij​ρCAij​=rCAij​+ICAij​+TCAij​+ϵCAij​​
(5)

3  Linearization about the master reference station

Given the known IBAij​ and ICAij​, the rover double-difference ionosphere IuAij​ is estimated as

IuAij​=Iui​−IAi​−(Iuj​−IAj​)=FIi​(ru​,ri)−FIi​(rA​,ri)−(FIj​(ru​,rj)−FIj​(rA​,rj))IBAij​=IBi​−IAi​−(IBj​−IAj​)=FIi​(rB​,ri)−FIi​(rA​,ri)−(FIj​(rB​,rj)−FIj​(rA​,rj))ICAij​=ICi​−IAi​−(ICj​−IAj​)=FIi​(rC​,ri)−FIi​(rA​,ri)−(FIj​(rC​,rj)−FIj​(rA​,rj))​
(6)

Expanding FIi​(rB​,ri) and FIi​(rC​,ri) as Taylor series about rA​ and neglecting the higher-order terms gives

FIi​(rB​,ri)=FIi​(rA​,ri)+∂rAT​∂FIi​(rA​,ri)​⋅(rB​−rA​)FIi​(rC​,ri)=FIi​(rA​,ri)+∂rAT​∂FIi​(rA​,ri)​⋅(rC​−rA​)​
(7)

and, likewise, for FIj​(rB​,rj) and FIj​(rC​,rj):

FIj​(rB​,rj)=FIj​(rA​,rj)+∂rAT​∂FIj​(rA​,rj)​⋅(rB​−rA​)FIj​(rC​,rj)=FIj​(rA​,rj)+∂rAT​∂FIj​(rA​,rj)​⋅(rC​−rA​)​
(8)

Substituting (6) and (7) into (5) yields

IBAij​=(∂rAT​∂FIi​(rA​,ri)​−∂rAT​∂FIj​(rA​,rj)​)⋅(rB​−rA​)ICAij​=(∂rAT​∂FIi​(rA​,ri)​−∂rAT​∂FIj​(rA​,rj)​)⋅(rC​−rA​)​
(9)

that is,

[IBAij​ICAij​​]=[(rB​−rA​)T(rC​−rA​)T​]⋅χIij​(∂rAT​∂FIi​(rA​,ri)​−∂rAT​∂FIj​(rA​,rj)​)T​​
(10)

where the column χIij​ is the double-difference ionospheric gradient. Expanding FIi​(ru​,ri) and FIj​(ru​,rj) about rA​ in the same way,

FIi​(ru​,ri)=FIi​(rA​,ri)+∂rAT​∂FIi​(rA​,ri)​⋅(ru​−rA​)FIj​(ru​,rj)=FIj​(rA​,rj)+∂rAT​∂FIj​(rA​,rj)​⋅(ru​−rA​)​
(11)

gives

IuAij​=(∂rAT​∂FIi​(rA​,ri)​−∂rAT​∂FIj​(rA​,rj)​)⋅(ru​−rA​)=(ru​−rA​)T⋅χIij​
(12)

that is, the rover double-difference ionosphere equals the projection of the gradient χIij​ onto the rover–master baseline vector.

4  Tropospheric delays

The same treatment applied to the tropospheric delay gives

[TBAij​TCAij​​]=[(rB​−rA​)T(rC​−rA​)T​]⋅χTij​(∂rAT​∂FTi​(rA​,ri)​−∂rAT​∂FTj​(rA​,rj)​)T​​
(13)

and

TuAij​=(∂rAT​∂FTi​(rA​,ri)​−∂rAT​∂FTj​(rA​,rj)​)⋅(ru​−rA​)=(ru​−rA​)T⋅χTij​
(14)

5  Virtual pseudorange observations

Suppose that a virtual reference station V is placed near the rover, still using A as the master reference station. The double-difference delays at V follow directly from the gradients:

IVAij​=(rV​−rA​)T⋅χIij​TVAij​=(rV​−rA​)T⋅χTij​​
(15)

and the VRS double-difference pseudorange observation equation is

ρVAij​=rVAij​+IVAij​+TVAij​+ϵVAij​
(16)

Forming the V–A and u–A double differences of the pseudoranges gives

ρVi​−ρAi​−(ρVj​−ρAj​)=rVi​−rAi​−(rVj​−rAj​)+IVAij​+TVAij​+ϵVAij​ρui​−ρAi​−(ρuj​−ρAj​)=rui​−rAi​−(ruj​−rAj​)+IuAij​+TuAij​+ϵuAij​​
(17)

Expanding rui​ and ruj​ with rV​ and re-grouping the delay terms,

ρui​−ρAi​−(ρuj​−ρAj​)=rui​−(rVi​+(rAi​−rVi​))−(ruj​−(rVj​+(rAj​−rVj​)))+(IuVij​+IuAij​−IuVij​)+(TuVij​+TuAij​−TuVij​)+ϵuVij​​
(18)

which can be written as

ρui​−ρVi​ρAi​+(rVi​−rAi​)+IVAij​+TVAij​​​−(ρuj​−ρVj​ρAj​+(rVj​−rAj​)​​)=rui​−rVi​−(ruj​−rVj​)+IuVij​+TuVij​+ϵuVij​
(19)

From the above, the virtual pseudorange observations are

ρVi​=ρAi​+(rVi​−rAi​)+IVAij​+TVAij​ρVj​=ρAj​+(rVj​−rAj​)​
(20)

Taking satellite 1 as the reference satellite of the VRS, its virtual observations are

​ρV1​ρV2​⋮ρVn​​​=​ρA1​+(rV1​−rA1​)ρA2​+(rV2​−rA2​)+IVA21​+TVA21​⋮ρAn​+(rVn​−rAn​)+IVAn1​+TVAn1​​​
(21)

If the rover uses satellite 2 as its own reference satellite, the double-difference pseudorange equation formed between the rover and the VRS is

ρu1​−(ρA1​+(rV1​−rA1​))−(ρu2​−(ρA2​+(rV2​−rA2​)+IVA21​+TVA21​))=ru1​−rV1​−(ru2​−rV2​)+IuV12​+TuV12​+ϵuV12​​
(22)

6  Equivalence with the rover–master double differences

Expanding (21) with the definitions (19) and (20),

ρu1​−ρA1​−(ρu2​−ρA2​)=ru1​−rV1​−(ru2​−rV2​)+(rV1​−rA1​)−(rV2​−rA2​)+IuV12​−IVA21​+TuV12​−TVA21​+ϵuV12​=ru1​−rA1​−(ru2​−rA2​)+IuA12​+TuA12​+ϵuA12​​
(23)

For any other satellite, e.g. satellite 3,

ρu3​−(ρA3​+(rV3​−rA3​)+IVA31​+TVA31​)−(ρu2​−(ρA2​+(rV2​−rA2​)+IVA21​+TVA21​))=ru3​−rV3​−(ru2​−rV2​)+IuV32​+TuV32​+ϵuV32​​
(24)
ρu3​−ρA3​−(ρu2​−ρA2​)=ru3​−rV3​−(ru2​−rV2​)+IuV32​+TuV32​+(rV3​−rA3​)+IVA31​+TVA31​−(rV2​−rA2​)−IVA21​−TVA21​+ϵuV32​=ru3​−rA3​−(ru2​−rA2​)+IuV32​+IVA31​−IVA21​+TuV32​+TVA31​−TVA21​+ϵuV32​=ru3​−rA3​−(ru2​−rA2​)+IuA32​+TuA32​​
(25)

and the delay terms reduce as

IuV32​+IVA31​−IVA21​=Iu3​−IV3​−(Iu2​−IV2​)+(IV3​−IA3​−(IV1​−IA1​))−(IV2​−IA2​−(IV1​−IA1​))=Iu3​−IA3​−(Iu2​−IA2​)=IuA32​​
(26)

By induction, the full set of rover–VRS double differences

​ρuV12​=ruV12​+IuV12​+TuV12​+ϵuV12​ρuV32​=ruV32​+IuV32​+TuV32​+ϵuV32​⋮ρuVn2​=ruVn2​+IuVn2​+TuVn2​+ϵuVn2​​​≡​ρuA12​=ruA12​+IuA12​+TuA12​+ϵuA12​ρuA32​=ruA32​+IuA32​+TuA32​+ϵuA32​⋮ρuAn2​=ruAn2​+IuAn2​+TuAn2​+ϵuAn2​​​
(27)

is equivalent to the set of rover–master double differences referred to satellite 2. Feeding the virtual observations (20) to a single-baseline RTK filter is therefore equivalent to processing the network solution directly at the rover.

Suppose now that n reference stations B1​,B2​,…,Bn​ operate around the master reference station A, each of them forming a baseline with A:

7  Network solution in the ENU frame

For the double-difference ionospheres of these baselines,

​IB1​Aij​IB2​Aij​IB3​Aij​⋮IBn​Aij​​​=​(rB1​​−rA​)T(rB2​​−rA​)T(rB3​​−rA​)T⋮(rBn​​−rA​)T​​⋅χIij​(∂rAT​∂FIi​(rA​,ri)​−∂rAT​∂FIj​(rA​,rj)​)T​​
(28)

To express χIij​ in the local ENU frame, let S be the rotation matrix from the ECEF frame to the topocentric coordinate system of the master station A. Inserting ST⋅S=I,

​IB1​Aij​IB2​Aij​IB3​Aij​⋮IBn​Aij​​​=​(rB1​​−rA​)T(rB2​​−rA​)T(rB3​​−rA​)T⋮(rBn​​−rA​)T​​⋅ST⋅IS​​⋅χIij​(∂rAT​∂FIi​(rA​,ri)​−∂rAT​∂FIj​(rA​,rj)​)T​​
(29)

Defining LIij​, the geometry matrix H and the ENU gradient χI,ENUij​ as

LIij​​IB1​Aij​IB2​Aij​IB3​Aij​⋮IBn​Aij​​​​​=H​(S⋅(rB1​​−rA​))T(S⋅(rB2​​−rA​))T(S⋅(rB3​​−rA​))T⋮(S⋅(rBn​​−rA​))T​​​​⋅χI,ENUij​S⋅(∂rAT​∂FIi​(rA​,ri)​−∂rAT​∂FIj​(rA​,rj)​)T​​
(30)

the observation model becomes

LIij​=H⋅χI,ENUij​
(31)

χI,ENUij​ contains the double-difference ionospheric gradients in the east, north and up directions. The least-squares estimate of (30) is

χI,ENUij​=(HT⋅H)−1⋅HT⋅LIij​
(32)

The double-difference ionosphere of the virtual station V is finally computed as

IVAij​=(rV​−rA​)T⋅χIij​=rENUVA​(S⋅(rV​−rA​))T​​⋅(HT⋅H)−1⋅HT⋅LIij​=((HT⋅H)−1⋅HT⋅LIij​)T⋅rENUVA​
(33)

and, in the same way, for the double-difference troposphere:

TVAij​=(rV​−rA​)T⋅χTij​=((HT⋅H)−1⋅HT⋅LTij​)T⋅rENUVA​
(34)

8  Virtual carrier-phase observations

The derivation for the carrier-phase observations proceeds along the same lines. The carrier-phase observation equation is

φui​=rui​+cdtu​−cdti−Iui​+Tui​+Nui​+εui​φAi​=rAi​+cdtA​−cdti−IAi​+TAi​+NAi​+εAi​φBi​=rBi​+cdtB​−cdti−IBi​+TBi​+NBi​+εBi​φCi​=rCi​+cdtC​−cdti−ICi​+TCi​+NCi​+εCi​​
(35)

Taking satellite j as the reference satellite and A as the master reference station, the double-difference carrier-phase observation equations are

φuAij​=ruAij​−IuAij​+TuAij​+NuAij​+ϵuAij​φBAij​=rBAij​−IBAij​+TBAij​+NBAij​+ϵBAij​φCAij​=rCAij​−ICAij​+TCAij​+NCAij​+ϵCAij​​
(36)

As with the virtual pseudoranges, the virtual carrier-phase observations are

φVi​=φAi​+(rVi​−rAi​)−IVAij​+TVAij​φVj​=φAj​+(rVj​−rAj​)​
(37)

and, with satellite 1 as the VRS reference satellite,

​φV1​φV2​⋮φVn​​​=​φA1​+(rV1​−rA1​)φA2​+(rV2​−rA2​)−IVA21​+TVA21​⋮φAn​+(rVn​−rAn​)−IVAn1​+TVAn1​​​
(38)

9  Second-order extension

If required, FIi​(ru​,ri) and FIj​(ru​,rj) can be expanded as Taylor series to second order:

FIi​(ru​,ri)=FIi​(rA​,ri)+∂rAT​∂FIi​(rA​,ri)​⋅(ru​−rA​)+(ru​−rA​)T⋅∂rA​∂rA​∂2FIi​(rA​,ri)​⋅(ru​−rA​)FIj​(ru​,rj)=FIj​(rA​,rj)+∂rAT​∂FIj​(rA​,rj)​⋅(ru​−rA​)+(ru​−rA​)T⋅∂rA​∂rA​∂2FIj​(rA​,rj)​⋅(ru​−rA​)​
(39)

The rover double-difference ionosphere then becomes

IuAij​=(∂rAT​∂FIi​(rA​,ri)​−∂rAT​∂FIj​(rA​,rj)​)⋅(ru​−rA​)+(ru​−rA​)T⋅(∂rA​∂rA​∂2FIi​(rA​,ri)​−∂rA​∂rA​∂2FIj​(rA​,rj)​)⋅(ru​−rA​)=(ru​−rA​)T⋅(∂rAT​∂FIi​(rA​,ri)​−∂rAT​∂FIj​(rA​,rj)​)T+(ru​−rA​)T⋅(∂rA​∂rA​∂2FIi​(rA​,ri)​−∂rA​∂rA​∂2FIj​(rA​,rj)​)⋅(ru​−rA​)​
(40)
=(ru​−rA​)T⋅χIij​(∂rAT​∂FIi​(rA​,ri)​−∂rAT​∂FIj​(rA​,rj)​)T​​+(ru​−rA​)T⋅ψIij​(∂rA​∂rA​∂2FIi​(rA​,ri)​−∂rA​∂rA​∂2FIj​(rA​,rj)​)​​⋅(ru​−rA​)
(41)

Neglecting the correlation of the gradient between the horizontal directions,

ψIij​=∂rA​∂rA​∂2FIi​(rA​,ri)​−∂rA​∂rA​∂2FIj​(rA​,rj)​≈​a000b000c​​
(42)

so that

IuAij​=(ru​−rA​)T⋅χIij​+τuA​[(ru​−rA​)x2​(ru​−rA​)y2​(ru​−rA​)z2​]​​⋅​abc​​
(43)

The master reference station A again forms the baselines AB1​,AB2​,…,ABn​ with the surrounding stations. For their double-difference ionospheres,

LIij​​IB1​Aij​IB2​Aij​IB3​Aij​⋮IBn​Aij​​​​​=Φ​(S⋅(rB1​​−rA​))T(S⋅(rB2​​−rA​))T(S⋅(rB3​​−rA​))T(S⋅(rBn​​−rA​))T​τB1​A​τB2​A​τB3​A​⋮τBn​A​​​​​⋅​χI,ENUij​abc​​
(44)

i.e.

LIij​=Φ⋅​χI,ENUij​abc​​
(45)

The least-squares estimate of (44) is

​χI,ENUij​abc​​=(HT⋅H)−1⋅HT⋅LIij​
(46)

The double-difference ionosphere of the virtual station V is then

IVAij​=(rV​−rA​)T⋅χIij​+(ru​−rA​)T⋅(ru​−rA​)⋅[abc]T=(S⋅(rV​−rA​))T⋅χI,ENUij​+τVA​⋅[abc]T=[(S⋅(rV​−rA​))TτVA​]⋅(ΦT⋅Φ)−1⋅ΦT⋅LIij​​
(47)

The troposphere is handled in exactly the same way.
